name: Business email compromise
summary: An attacker takes over an executive or finance mailbox, hides their activity with inbox rules and uses the trusted account to redirect a payment.

attack_path.description: Credential-phishing link leads to a fake sign-in page; MFA is bypassed through repeated push prompts or a stolen session cookie.
Inbox rules forward or hide messages so the real user does not notice replies from the attacker's targets.
The attacker reads invoices and vendor threads to learn payment processes.
Phishing is sent internally from the trusted account and a vendor payment is redirected to an attacker-controlled bank account.

key_decisions: How quickly the bank can be contacted to attempt a payment recall
Whether other mailboxes or the identity provider are also compromised
Whether customers or vendors whose data was in the mailbox must be notified
What payment verification controls change after the incident
